source_search_execution_summary.stop_reason: Maximum iterations (2) reached. The search has surfaced a strong, multi-layered set of authoritative source candidates: (1) The CDPH VBDS Annual Report 2024 (westnile.ca.gov/pdfs/VBDSAnnualReport24.pdf) — the highest-authority source, providing county-level WNV case incidence for 2024 across all California counties, enabling population of subnational_location, locality, cases_confirmed, and date_reported fields; (2) CDPH News Release NR24-27 (cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OPA/Pages/NR24-27.aspx) — reporting 63 human WNV cases and 6 deaths for 2024, with evidence quote potential; (3) CDPH 2024 Year-End Monthly Summary PDF (cdph.ca.gov) — providing WNV case type breakdowns (neuroinvasive: 103, non-neuroinvasive: 30, asymptomatic: 20, total: 153) with monthly columns; (4) Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District 2024 activity page (glamosquito.org) — providing locality-level August 2024 mosquito pool data with specific dates (8/7/2024, 8/22/2024, 8/29/2024) and neighborhood-level granularity; (5) contracosta.news article (2024-10-01) republishing CDPH figures (63 cases, 6 deaths) with evidence quote; (6) CDC Historic Data page (cdc.gov/west-nile-virus/data-maps/historic-data.html) — ArboNET state-level data for cross-validation; (7) kernpublichealth.com, ruhealth.org, nevadacountyca.gov — county-level public health sources for Kern, Riverside, and Nevada counties. Key remaining gap: August-specific monthly case counts are not confirmed from snippets alone (the CDPH year-end PDF has monthly columns but the August column values are not visible in the snippet; the VBDS Annual Report provides 2024 annual totals by county but not month-specific breakdowns). However, these sources are the correct candidates for extraction — the gap is a data extraction challenge, not a source discovery gap. Additional searching is unlikely to surface sources with better August-specific granularity than the CDPH VBDS Annual Report and the westnile.ca.gov portal, which are the definitive California WNV surveillance sources.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: HIGH. All major target field categories are covered by identified source candidates: (a) disease/country/subnational_location — all sources; (b) locality — VBDS Annual Report 2024 (county-level table), glamosquito.org (neighborhood-level LA data with August 2024 dates); (c) date_reported — CDPH NR24-27 (2024 season), contracosta.news (2024-10-01 dateline), glamosquito.org (specific August dates); (d) cases_confirmed/cases_probable/cases_unspecified — CDPH VBDS Annual Report 2024 (county breakdown), CDPH year-end monthly PDF (type breakdown: neuroinvasive 103, non-neuroinvasive 30, asymptomatic 20); (e) deaths — CDPH NR24-27 (6 deaths), CDPH year-end total (153 cases); (f) hospitalizations — partially covered (CDPH sources may include this; not confirmed in snippets); (g) source_url/source_type/evidence_quote — multiple sources with quotable snippets. The primary gap is August-specific (vs. annual) case counts, which is a data extraction challenge inherent to how CDPH publishes surveillance data, not a source discovery gap.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: HIGH. The dominant sources are official California state government agencies: CDPH (cdph.ca.gov) and the California WNV surveillance portal (westnile.ca.gov), both operated by CDPH/CDFA. The CDPH VBDS Annual Report 2024 is the gold-standard annual surveillance document. The CDC ArboNET historic data page provides federal-level cross-validation. County-level sources (kernpublichealth.com, ruhealth.org, nevadacountyca.gov, glamosquito.org) are official or quasi-official local public health entities. The contracosta.news article is a secondary source but explicitly republishes CDPH figures. The s47353.pcdn.co PDF is a 2023 document and should be deprioritized. Facebook results should be excluded. No peer-reviewed literature was surfaced, which is expected for a one-month 2024 window.
